title: Terraform module: monitoring assembly with retention and health probes
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Scope: Implement a reusable Terraform module to provision a production-grade monitoring assembly for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will support Kubernetes-hosted Prometheus and Grafana (via Helm or upstream manifests), an OpenTelemetry Collector deployment (collector + pipeline config), and a pluggable log-shipping component (Fluent Bit or Vector) with S3-compatible long-term storage and KMS-encrypted buckets. The module must be usable both in Redwood Private clusters and in customer-on-prem clusters with minimal overrides.

Goals/Acceptance criteria:
- Single Terraform module with clear inputs for namespace, chart versions, retention windows, storage backends, and TLS/KMS config.
- Prometheus deployed with node/endpoint scrape configs, ServiceMonitors for our common components, and retention policy configurable per-environment.
- Grafana deployed with provisioning for dashboards (JSON from repo), RBAC for viewer/editor roles, and integration to internal SSO.
- OTEL Collector configured with resource-aware replicas, CPU/memory defaults, and an HTTP health endpoint compatible with k8s readiness/liveness probes.
- Log shipping component supports per-namespace tails, structured parsing, and writes to an encrypted S3 bucket. Long-term retention policies configurable and compatible with our archival workflow.
- Upgrade strategy: module supports canary rollouts using k8s deployment annotations + a canary-level toggle; lifecycle hooks to drain and reattach PVCs where applicable.
- Health checks: automated k8s readiness/liveness probes, cross-component synthetic checks (prometheus rule that evaluates collector and log forwarder metrics), and a Terraform-driven prober resource that can run lightweight canary validation post-upgrade.
- CI pipeline: unit tests for tf plan, terratest for manifest generation, and a staged apply in a short-lived cluster for each release.
- Documentation: Confluence design doc, runbook for failed upgrades, and a migration checklist for existing VPC observability installs.

Design decisions and trade-offs: We evaluated two delivery patterns: (A) heavy Terraform with Helm provider managing everything, or (B) Terraform that templates YAML and relies on a GitOps operator (ArgoCD) to apply. We landed on (B) for the following reasons: easier rollback, separation of concerns with infra vs k8s desired state, and better visibility in cluster git history. However the module will still expose a \"helm_mode\" toggle for customers that require direct Helm usage.

Storage/retention: use S3-compatible backend with server-side encryption via KMS. Retention lifecycle policies will be defined by the module, but final archival decisions are delegated to the customer. For intermediate Prometheus TSDB retention, default is 15d for non-prod and 90d for prod, but configurable via input variables.

Security: least-privilege IAM roles for write access to buckets, KMS key aliasing pattern, and option to inject an existing key. All sensitive values are expected to come from the Secret Store module and never inline in TF variables.

Rollout strategy: Canary toggle + CI validation that runs a prober job (see acceptance tests) which verifies scrape targets, verifies collector pipelines can export to our staging endpoint, and verifies logs appear in S3. If prober fails, the module will not proceed with final step.

Deliverables:
- sources/infra/modules/monitoring-assembly (tf module)
- example overlay for private (VPC) clusters
- terratest suite and GH Actions workflow
- Confluence design doc and runbook

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Collector memory spikes on high-cardinality traces. Mitigation: provide resource autoscaler guidance, default sampling, and a collector default pipeline that downsamples spans at high throughput.
- Risk: Breaking customer dashboards during Grafana upgrades. Mitigation: Grafana provisioning uses side-by-side dashboard namespaces and scripted migration utilities; we will run a dry-run compare in CI before apply.
